# Worked Instances {#sec-instances}

The trichotomy of @sec-theorem is stated over append-only records
specifically. This section introduces its companion theorem, states it
over a more general structure, and works the framework on real cases —
a generality demonstration, not a survey of examples chosen after the
fact.

## The verification ceiling: a companion, not a corollary

Generalize from a single append-only record to a **well-founded
justification structure**: a directed acyclic graph of artifacts, each
either a leaf or carrying a derived record naming its own inputs
, together with a fail-closed classification of every artifact
into one of four buckets relative to an admitted policy $P$ and an
evidence snapshot $\sigma$: $\lean{closed}$, meaning the artifact's
establishment is fully accounted for; $\lean{establishGap}$ and $\lean{attestGap}$,
naming which half is missing; and $\lean{import}$, the bucket a genesis seed
always lands in.

Two species of evidence do that accounting, and the distinction between
them is the one the whole display turns on. A **corroboration** is an
admitted party's re-verification of an artifact against its own
committed content — a check anyone else could re-run. A **vouch** is an
admitted party's keyed judgment binding the artifact to the principal it
names — testimony, which no one can re-run. Corroborations are evidence
a verifier could in principle reproduce; vouches are exactly the trust
the rest of this paper is about. Acyclicity is by construction rather than by
assumption: a node's inputs are syntactic subterms of the node, so no
artifact can name itself, transitively or otherwise, and the structure
cannot express a circular justification to have to exclude.

Two derived quantities carry the accounting. The **trust surface**
$T(a)$ is $a$'s dependency closure minus its $\lean{closed}$ members — every
node landing in one of the three residue buckets. The
**assumption basis** $B(a)$ is the policy-admitted evidence those
non-residue classifications actually rest on. $\lean{Total}$ names
the state in which every non-seed member of the closure is $\lean{closed}$
.

**Joining the two worlds.** The accounting vocabulary above — artifacts,
buckets, policies — and the scheme vocabulary of @sec-model share no
object either is defined in terms of, so a statement about the trust
surface says nothing about evidence schemes until the two are linked.
The link is a **record realization** for a closure
: a map $\mathit{recordOf}$ from artifacts to
records satisfying two conditions **within one artifact $a$'s dependency
closure**, and nowhere else — **(R1)** for $n$ in that closure, building
on an artifact extends its record, $m \in \mathit{depclosure}\ n
\Rightarrow \mathit{recordOf}\ m \sqsubseteq \mathit{recordOf}\ n$; and
**(R2)** within that closure, an artifact is a genesis seed exactly when
its record commits no prior entries.

The scoping is load-bearing, not fastidious. Stated over every node of
the type, (R2) is refutable — the type admits a node flagged as a seed
with an arbitrary identifier, which no builder constructs but the
constructors permit. Scoped to a closure, it becomes exactly what a real
builder's own structure can discharge.

The neutral core cannot supply this and should not. $\mathit{Entry}$ is
opaque by construction (@sec-model), so no map into $\Record$ is
definable there at all; the realization is the domain's to provide,
bundled as a structure the way a commitment is. Given one, "$S$
establishes artifact $m$ without admission" becomes a genuine relation —
$S$ is snapshot-sound *and* accepts a certificate for $m$'s own record
— whose two halves are consumed in a single step
.

::: {.theorem}
**The verification ceiling**. For such a structure
with a record realization, under an explicit underdetermination
hypothesis on the domain's binding claim:

(i) **Gate.** The binding or genuineness claim admits no snapshot-sound
 evidence scheme over any commitment.

(ii) **Seed junction.** For *every* scheme, every seed in the closure is
 undischarged and lies in the trust surface
.

(iii) **Minimality.** $\lean{Total}$ holds *if and only if* the trust surface
 equals the closure's seeds. That equality is
 the *ceiling*: a system achieving it cannot be improved on, and
 reaching it is not merely implied by totality but equivalent to it.

(iv) **Completeness.** Under $\lean{Total}$, every non-seed member of the
 closure carries both evidence species — a corroboration and a vouch
 — in the assumption basis. Nothing is
 silently trusted.
:::

All four are proved, and (iii) is a biconditional rather than the single
implication a ceiling display needs.

The per-member force of (iv) is sharpened by a companion fact: a closed
artifact's own declaration never suffices to close it, since closing
requires evidence admitted against that artifact's own identity and
payload. Nothing an artifact says
about itself counts as evidence for itself.

Parts (iii) and (iv) are conditioned on $\lean{Total}$, which raises the
obvious question: can admitting more evidence undo it? No — totality
survives every extension of the evidence snapshot, unconditionally
. The direction is worth noticing. Growth of the
*record* can defeat a claim, which is exactly @sec-cell-table's T3
flavour; growth of the *evidence* cannot defeat the accounting kept over
it.

This remains a **companion** and not a corollary. It shares the gate;
everything else — the classification, the two evidence species, the
accounting, the junction — is its own machinery, proved over vocabulary
$\TTsnap$/$\TTend$ never mentions.

The underdetermination hypothesis is likewise a **modeling hypothesis,
never a theorem and never an axiom**: it is the domain's own fiber
witness, that one committed record can arise under two ambient contexts
with different binding verdicts. It is carried explicitly as an argument
on every theorem that needs it. Proving it would mean fixing a concrete
claim and a concrete pair of contexts, which is precisely what each
instance is responsible for asserting for itself.

## Two instantiations, because one instance is a special case

The ceiling is instantiated twice, over genuinely disjoint domains,
because one instance demonstrating generality is a special case wearing
a general theorem's clothes, while two — chosen to stress
*complementary* failure cells rather than the same one twice — is the
beginning of a theory. Each instance names the cells it exercises, so
the complementarity is checkable rather than asserted. The cell labels
are those of @tbl-cells.

**Identity.** An identity system whose record is a chain of key events
and whose genesis is a single binding commitment.
The mechanized chain is structural — an ordered sequence of events, each
naming a principal — with no hash function in it; what the instance
exercises is the accounting, not the cryptography. It exercises **T1** — its genesis binding claim
fails determination under the domain's fiber hypothesis, since
byte-identical chains can arise under honest custody or under
impersonation — and **T3**, through the split-view example below. Its
sharpest statement is not the ceiling instantiation but a stronger,
domain-specific one: under $\lean{Total}$, the trust surface of a chain is
*exactly* the genesis binding and nothing else
, which follows from splitting the chain's
dependency closure into its derived nodes and its single seed
. This instance has no conditional frontier — no
forced-generator or Rice-theoretic tightness result stands between the
model and the theorem — which makes it the cleanest evidence that the
completeness and minimality machinery is not build-specific.

**Its realization is constructed, not assumed.** The instance builds one
rather than positing it: an artifact's record is the prefix
of an ambient append-only log determined by that artifact's identifier,
and (R1) and (R2) are discharged by induction on the chain's own
structure under two
hypotheses about the caller's event list — that identifiers do not
increase as one descends from the chain's head toward its genesis, and
that identifier zero is reserved for genesis. A third hypothesis, that
identifiers distinguish artifacts, is carried and not discharged.

The realization therefore *varies* with the artifact: distinct
identifiers get distinct records, which is what (R1) and (R2) need. It
does not read the artifact's payload, and the log it indexes into is
supplied by the caller rather than derived from the chain — so what is
proved is that this domain's structure supports a realization, not that
its key events determine one.

**A light source-integrity instance.** Its build-domain name, wherever
the general ceiling is instantiated to source integrity, is the **surety
ceiling**. It exercises **T1** — genuineness of a
source artifact fails determination under the same shape of fiber
hypothesis — and **T2**, since the certifiability failure it inherits is
committed-generator degeneracy, which rests on cited mathematics rather
than mechanized proof (@sec-cell-table). Between the two instances,
then, T1, T2, and T3 all have a witness in some instance.

This second instance is deliberately light: an abstract, vouch-shaped
establishment predicate over source classes, with zero frontier
machinery — no format or parse gates, no corroboration quorum, no
forced-generator tightness result. **The full empirical treatment is a
follow-up paper, cited and not included.** Folding it in would mix
conditional, prose-grade frontier content into a paper whose epistemic
grade is otherwise uniformly machine-checked, and that uniformity is
what the split protects.

**Its realization is content-neutral, and the asymmetry with identity is
real.** This instance takes the general construction,
which satisfies (R1) and (R2) unconditionally — it is also what
establishes that those two conditions are jointly satisfiable at all —
but distinguishes artifacts only by how many entries they commit. The
light payload carries no chain-like structure to discharge a
content-bearing realization from, and building one belongs to the
follow-up rather than here. So the ceiling holds at this instance over a
realization that does not depend on what the records say. One instance
exhibits a content-carrying realization discharged from its own
structure; the other instantiates over a neutral one. What the two
jointly witness is *axis coverage* — T1 with T3, and T1 with T2 — which
is the claim @sec-cell-table makes and the only one made here.

Neither instance imports a computability library — the ceiling's content
is accounting and impossibility, and neither needs one. Across every
declaration in the ceiling's own development, the axioms used are Lean's
$\lean{propext}$ and $\lean{Quot.sound}$, together with the model's declared opacities
wherever a statement reaches into the scheme world; choice is not among
them.

**Both instances are non-vacuous**, each carrying four concrete
witnesses over finite types, listed in Appendix A. The sharpest
shows the accounting genuinely depends on admitted testimony rather than
deriving everything from the gate — a policy admitting no vouchers
forbids every non-seed $\lean{Total}$.

## The extended worked example: split-view, resolved without a fourth axis

A verifier facing two different views of what is claimed to be the same
append-only log — a *split-view*, or equivocation, attack — looks at
first glance like it needs a fourth axis. Neither determination,
certifiability, nor monotonicity obviously names "my two sources
disagree." It does not. The attack decomposes without remainder into two
claims the trichotomy already owns.

**Per-verifier**: "my anchor commits a prefix of the canonical record."
For a fixed anchor this claim is determined, monotone, and certifiable
*over the canonical record*; the verifier's actual difficulty is that
its only access to the canonical record is the anchor itself. The trust
spent is the admitted anchor — an entailment move against $P$
(@sec-cell-table), not a new axis.

**Cross-verifier**: "the two views I have been shown are consistent with
each other," where consistency means one view extends the other
. Posed over the joint record of shown views, this
claim is determined and certifiable — a consistency proof is literally
its certificate — and **non-monotone**: two views consistent today can
diverge tomorrow, and the mechanization exhibits exactly that flip
(over a two-element alphabet, which such a divergence provably
requires). This is the monotonicity-failure case,
$\EON$ applies directly, and the cure coordinates of @sec-cell-table
predict the deployed defenses verbatim: entailment via a witness quorum
or gossip protocol, cosigned
checkpoints, restriction to "consistent as of time $t$," or an accepted
expiry window.

A sharper fact falls out for free. Divergence, once it exists, is
*permanent* under further extension of both views: two records that
disagree at a position keep disagreeing there forever
. So *equivocation* is monotone and affirmable —
its evidence, once obtained, endures — while *honesty* is refutative,
never provable forever, only falsifiable at the next check. That
asymmetry is why gossip protocols work at all, and why "this log is
honest" can only be held as expiring, snapshot-grade confidence rather
than an enduring one. The framework does not merely classify the attack;
it explains the shape of the field's actual defense against it.

A fourth axis would have to make verification fail for a claim that is
determined, certifiable, *and* monotone. Neither component of the
split-view decomposition does that. This is the strongest available
validation of the three-axis count against a real adversarial case,
rather than against a textbook one.
